title: The 30 recovery.v_ace_* views have no row in the Ownership Map, so the model gives them no owner
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Conceptual Data Model v6.xlsx
description: v6 holds 122 entities: 88 Workbench tables, the 4 extension tables and the 30 ACE source views, and it has no owner column at all. The Ownership Map sheet Tables has 93 rows and every one is a Workbench table, so the 30 views have no owner row to take a value from, although they are 30 of the 122 entities and the only read path the realignment keeps into ACE.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 line 1074 (SQL: ACE DB views, SELECT recovery.v_ace_* (30 views)), line 700 (only rwb-source-data reads the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views) and line 843 (SQL view: only rwb-source-data, read-only login, 30 views, statement timeout); Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables, 93 rows, first column holds table names only (account_ext to write_off) and no v_ace_* name; v6 Entities row 2 (122 entities: 88 Workbench tables, then the 4 extension tables, then the 30 ACE source views).
area: Data / ownership of the ACE source views
proposed: Give all 30 views owning service P1 and target schema 'recovery (ACE, read-only view)', taken from Architecture v5 rather than the map, and add a Views sheet to the Ownership Map so the map stays the single source of owners.

title: The entity Payment match rule has no row in the Ownership Map and no target table
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Conceptual Data Model v6.xlsx
section: Entities (row Payment match rule) and the Reference and access subject area
description: v6 holds Payment match rule with 13 fields in DP14. The table is dropped by D-RCV-36 T10, so the Ownership Map, which lists target tables, has no row for it, and the realignment has to name an owner for a row that has no target table. The LDM already marks every one of its fields 'Retired by D-RCV-36'.
evidence: Decision Log v10 D-RCV-36 T10 (payment_match_rule is dropped and payment matching becomes the PAYMENT_MATCH package); the LDM v8 field descriptions of payment_match_rule carry 'Retired by D-RCV-36'; Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables has no payment_match_rule row, while rule_package and rule_package_version are there with owner P7; v6 Entities row Payment match rule.
area: Data / reference data and the rule registry
proposed: Keep the entity and all 13 fields, set owning service P7 and target schema rwb_decision, and record in the ownership basis that the table is retired and the rule lives in the PAYMENT_MATCH rule package.

title: No entity is owned by S1 rwb-valuation, although Architecture v5 gives S1 the valuations and the route decision
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Conceptual Data Model v6.xlsx
section: Service ownership (S1 row) and the Collateral and asset subject area
description: The Ownership Map assigns 93 tables to 18 services and the platform library. rwb-valuation owns none of them: the appraisal data is the read-only v_ace_valuation view and valuation_ext, both P1 under the map's own ruling, and the assets are S5. S1 therefore has no table, no schema content and no DB story of its own in this model, although Arch v5 gives it 'valuations, D6 route decision, route agent output'.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables: no row with owner S1; rows valuation_ext (owner P1) and listing and asset_sale (owner S5); Ownership Map v1 sheet Rulings row valuation_ext (ruling ASM-A6-tables-15 keeps valuation_ext with P1); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (S1 rwb-valuation owning valuations, D6 route decision, route agent output); v6 Entities rows Valuation extension and v_ace_valuation.
proposed: Record S1 as owning no entity in this version and let its DB story create the rwb_valuation schema with its Flyway baseline only; refer the definition of a rwb_valuation table, if one is wanted, to the S1 design review.

title: The entity called Rule is rule_row, and the model holds neither rule_package nor rule_package_version
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Conceptual Data Model v6.xlsx
section: Entities (row Rule) and the Reference and access subject area
description: v6 names the entity 'Rule', which is not a table name, and holds 18 fields. The LDM maps that name to rule_row. The two registry rows that the realignment makes central, rule_package and rule_package_version, are in the Ownership Map but not in the model, so one entity name needed resolving and two entities are absent.
evidence: LDM v8 dictionary row rule_row (entity 'Rule', 18 fields, 'One versioned routing rule or sentry') and rows rule_package (5 fields) and rule_package_version; Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables rows rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case, all owner P7, schema rwb_decision; Decision Log v10 D-RCV-36 T4 (rule_package_version with rollback) and T6 (rule_row stays the rule catalog); v6 Entities row Rule.
proposed: Resolve 'Rule' to rule_row in the ownership basis (done, owner P7) and add rule_package and rule_package_version as entities of P7 in the next version; no row of v6 is renamed.

title: The 104 relationships are single-schema references and the Ownership Map's FK cut sheet is empty
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Conceptual Data Model v6.xlsx
description: v6 draws 104 references as if one schema held every table. With one schema and one login per service, 59 of them now cross a service boundary: 11 already point at a read-only ACE view as a business key, and 48 are a Workbench table in one service pointing at a Workbench table in another, which cannot stay a foreign key. The Ownership Map has a sheet for that cut, and it holds no data row.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 sheet FK cuts: header row only (From table, From owner, To table, To owner, Becomes) and no data row; v6 Relationships row 2 (104 relationships, a reference to a v_ace_* view is a business key with no foreign key); Template and Rules R4 (schema and login per service) and DP-01 (never read another service's tables); Ownership Map sheet Services (19 schemas).
proposed: Cut the 48 table-to-table foreign keys to business-key columns, keep the 11 ACE view references as they are, and show all three cases per row in the Relationships sheet; each service's DB story creates no foreign key to another schema.

title: The four platform library tables have schema 'platform' in the map but are created in every service schema
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Conceptual Data Model v6.xlsx
section: Entities (Outbox event, Outbox delivery, Processed event, Idempotency key)
description: The map gives outbox_event, outbox_delivery, processed_event and idempotency_key owner PLT and schema 'platform', while the ruling on the same rows says they are library objects created in every service schema. A single target schema per entity cannot say both, so the column needed a wording of its own.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables rows outbox_event, outbox_delivery, processed_event and idempotency_key (owner PLT, schema platform) with the ruling 'library objects created in every service schema ... ASM-A6-tables-8'; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (every service: own schema with outbox and inbox) and slide 11 (transactional outbox); Template and Rules DP-09.
proposed: Write target schema 'every service schema (platform library object)' for the four rows, keep owner PLT, and record that each service's DB story creates its own copy.

title: Feature flags are 'Workbench' as system of record in the model but owned by the platform library
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Conceptual Data Model v6.xlsx
section: Entities (Feature flag, Feature flag change) in the Loads and operations subject area
description: v6 states 'Workbench' as the system of record of both feature-flag tables. The map moves them to the platform library under the default ruling, and P2 only serves the admin API. The preserved column and the new owner now disagree, which is left visible rather than edited.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables rows feature_flag and feature_flag_change (owner PLT, schema platform) and sheet Rulings row feature_flag (R-PREC default ruling, ASM-A6-tables-7, P2 serves the admin API); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (every service from the service template and shared libraries); v6 Entities rows Feature flag and Feature flag change, System of record 'Workbench'.
proposed: Keep column E word for word, add owner PLT and target schema 'platform library', and note in the next version that P2 serves the admin API against the library.

title: The Key sheet has no term for the five realignment concepts the new columns use
source: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Conceptual Data Model v6.xlsx
description: The Key defines 16 terms and values of v6: subject area, data product, entity, system of record, the four system-of-record values, the two cardinalities, the two standards and the ACE source view, extension table and business key. It has no term for an owning service, a target schema, the platform library, a cross-service reference or a service contract, which are the words of every new column.
evidence: v6 Key sheet rows 5 to 21 (16 rows) and row 2 (What each term and value means); v6 has no owning-service column anywhere; Template and Rules R4 and R5.5 (schema, login, topic and package per service) and Ownership Map v1 sheet Services (19 services, 19 schemas).
proposed: Append five Term rows at rows 22 to 26 and leave the 16 v6 rows unchanged.
